pairs.evidence: lib/foundry/store.ts:15 The forge store writes git-tracked index files (ledger.json, styles.json) but never stages, commits, stashes or opens worktrees; a search of lib/foundry for worktree, git stash, GIT_INDEX_FILE and git commit found nothing, so the subject's precondition of sessions committing in a shared checkout does not hold here - only the generic shared-resource technique applies, and it is conformant.

techniques.evidence: lib/foundry/runStore.ts:88 Scratch files are namespaced per process and call; the singular indices are gated by an exclusive-create lock that names its owner (by: "app") and has a stale rule (lib/diskTx.ts staleMs, outside the context), and a timeout returns a 503 telling the operator what to check instead of polling forever (catalogue.ts:243).
lib/foundry/fsPort.ts:12 Here "commit" means a multi-file write to disk, not a git commit, so there is no log to read back.
lib/foundry/store.ts:15 Nothing in the context touches the git staging index.
lib/foundry/store.ts:15 No stash, bulk add or reset; the files are left for a later git commit made elsewhere.
lib/foundry/fsPort.ts:12 No worktree creation or removal in this context.

pairs.evidence: packages/ui/src/board/commit.ts:20 The board's "commit" is a pure UI state machine for confirming a review packet, and its only concurrency control is a server revision with retry on conflict; a search of packages/ui/src for worktree, git stash, GIT_INDEX_FILE, git commit and git add found nothing, so no version-control technique has anything to govern here.

techniques.evidence: packages/ui/src/board/commit.ts:20 A packet commit flow (preview, token, confirm), not a git commit.
packages/ui/src/board/boardGate.ts:6 Optimistic concurrency over a server record, not arbitration of a machine resource shared between sessions.
